claim_decisions.statement: Source dated not stated reports: IAWASuR aims to benefit 75,000 people (51% women) across Anjouan, Mohéli and Grande Comore through watershed restoration, climate-resilient water infrastructure, climate-smart governance and institutional capacity-building.

gaps: Main read the UNICEF projection context and the publicly disclosed April 2025 PID. Current water insecurity must not be reduced to drought alone; infrastructure, oversight and maintenance are central.
The national rainwater share is not a Grand Moroni estimate. Flood returns and intended water beneficiaries are not evidence of long-term risk reduction or peace outcomes.

executive_assessment.text: Island water-source differences and named 2024 flood localities deepen local exposure; Grand Moroni's reliability and affordability deficits are distinct from national rainwater dependence.
Political-instability legacies and weak water institutions constrain capacity. Proposed three-island water measures and child-protection risks are not evaluated resilience or conflict outcomes.
